correctness.rationale: Every width-two rooted forest is uniquely a chain, two separate chains, or a single rooted fork with a unary stem and two arms. The directed-ideal cover counts yield the displayed bivariate polynomials, whose x/y monomial patterns separate shapes; their coefficients recover arm sums and products. Setting x=1 gives B=1+n y+m y^2 and the exact multiplicative fibre formula; straightforward subtraction and coprimality yield the 2n−1 odd-compositeness characterization. Two-variable counting rank-two separation follows by counting vertices of each incoming/outgoing cover degree. Independently built parent-array bitmask enumerator checked 173 canonical types through n=12, both-degree fingerprints and fibre counts; it is a finite diagnostic only.
